source_text:
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Τούτων δὲ οὕτως εὖ μάλα τετηρημένων, καὶ μὴν καὶ εἰς πέρας ἐξενηνεγμένων κατά γε τῷ νομοθέτῃ δοκοῦν, διελεύσεσθαί φησι καὶ οἱονεὶ πᾶσαν περινοστήσειν τὴν Αἰγυπτίων, καὶ διολλύναι μὲν τὰ πρωτότοκα, ποιήσειν δὲ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν ἐν τοῖς θεοῖς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, τουτέστι, πάντα τὸν παρ' αὐτοῖς ὑψηλόν τε καὶ ἐπηρμένον, καὶ ἐν τοῖς προσκυνουμένοις μονονουχὶ τεταγμένον διά γε τὴν δόξαν, ἐξαιτήσειν δίκας τῆς οὕτω σκληρᾶς καὶ ἀτάκτου γνώμης, καὶ τῆς ἄγαν ἀλαζονείας. Σκεπάσειν γε μὴν τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ ἐπηγγέλλετο, κατακεχρισμένων τῷ αἵματι τῶν φλιῶν, ὃ δὴ καὶ σημεῖον ὠνόμαζε τῆς πρὸς αὐτὸν οἰκειώσεως. «Ὄψομαι γὰρ, φησὶ, σημεῖον, καὶ σκεπάσω ὑμᾶς.» Θεοῦ γὰρ ἐπάγοντος ὀργὴν καὶ θυμὸν ἐπὶ πάντα ὑψηλὸν καὶ μετέωρον, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνὴν, καὶ θανάτῳ καταδικάζοντος τὸν ἀσελγῆ τε καὶ ἀλιτήριον, καὶ τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν εὐσεβείας ἀνακαταλήκτως ὀλιγωρήσαντα, διαδιδράσκουσι μόνοι καὶ ἀμοιροῦσι ποινῆς, οἱ καλῷ σημάντρῳ κατεσφραγισμένοι, καὶ ἐῤῥαντισμένοι τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Διεπύθου γὰρ λέγοντος, «Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται, ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν· ὁ δὲ μὴ πιστεύων, οὐκ ὄψεται τὴν ζωὴν, ἀλλ' ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ Θεοῦ μενεῖ ἐπ' αὐτόν.» Οὐκοῦν καὶ ζωῆς τῆς αἰωνίου μέτοχοι, καὶ Θεῷ τε καὶ Πατρὶ φίλοι τε καὶ γνώριμοι, καὶ θανάτου κρείττους, οἱ ἡγιασμένοι, διά γε τοῦ μετασχεῖν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κατὰ τρόπον δὲ δηλονότι τὸν μυστικὸν, καὶ αἵματι τῷ ἁγίῳ κατακεχρισμένοι. Χρῆναί γε μὴν ἀκαταλήκτως αὐτοὺς ἀποπεραίνειν ἐπείγεσθαι τὸν ἐπὶ τῷδε νόμον εὖ μάλα φησί. Καταλήξομεν γὰρ, οὔτι που τοῦ ἑορτάζειν ἐπὶ Χριστῷ, ζύμην ἀφανίζοντες ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων ὁρίων, τουτέστιν, ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς γῆς ἐν ᾗπερ ἂν ἔχοιμεν τὰς διατριβάς. Δεήσει γὰρ δὴ τοὺς διὰ πίστεως κεκλημένους εἰς δικαίωσιν τὴν διὰ Χριστοῦ, πνευματικῶς ἑορτάζοντας, μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ τοῦτο δρᾷν, κακίας τε καὶ πονηρίας, ἐκκαθαίροντας δὲ μᾶλλον τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, μεταπλάττεσθαι πρὸς τὸ ἄμεινον, καὶ νέον ἤδη πως ὁρᾶσθαι φύραμα, παγγενῆ τε καὶ πανοικὶ, καὶ τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ τῇ χώρᾳ, δι' οὗ σημαίνεται τῶν τὴν πίστιν παραδεδεγμένων πολλή τις οὖσα καὶ ἀναρίθμητος ἡ ὁσία πληθύς. Τὴν δέ γε πρώτην τῆς ἑβδομάδος ἡμέραν, ἁγίαν ἔφη διακεκλῆσθαι δεῖν, κλητὴν δὲ ἁγίαν καὶ τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐκεῖνο, οἶμαί που, παραδεικνὺς ὁ νόμος, ὅτι τῆς ἀνθρώπου ζωῆς ἅγιος μὲν ἦν ὁ ἐν ἀρχῇ χρόνος, ὡς ἐν τῷ προπάτορι τοῦ γένους Ἀδὰμ, οὔπω παραλύσαντι τὰ ἐντεταλμένα, καὶ τῶν θείων ἀλογήσαντι προσταγμάτων· ἅγιος δὲ καὶ πολὺ μείζων, ὁ ἐν ἐσχάτοις, τουτέστιν, ὁ ἐν Χριστῷ, ὅς ἐστι δεύτερος Ἀδὰμ, ἀναστοιχειῶν τὸ γένος ἐκ τῶν διὰ μέσου συμβεβηκότων, εἰς καινότητα ζωῇς, ἐν πνεύματι. Παρεγγυᾷ δὲ ὅτι καὶ σαββατίζειν ἀνάγκη κατὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἀποφοιτῶντας ἔργου παντός. Πρέποι γὰρ ἂν καὶ μάλα εἰκότως τοῖς διὰ πίστεως εἰσεληλα
pass_a_gloss: PALL.: You spoke excellently. CYR.: These things having been very well observed, and indeed carried out to the end according to what seems good to the lawgiver, he says he will go through and as it were go around all (the land) of the Egyptians, and destroy the firstborn, and do the vengeance on the gods of the Egyptians, that is, all the high and lifted-up among them, and ranked all but among the things worshiped on account of the glory, he will demand penalties for the so hard and disorderly judgment and the excessive boasting. But he promised to shelter the sons of Israel, the lintels having been anointed with the blood, which he also named a sign of the belonging to him. 'For I will see,' he says, 'a sign, and I will shelter you.' For God bringing wrath and anger upon everything high and lofty, according to the voice of the prophet, and condemning to death the licentious and sinful one, who has neglected unceasingly the reverence toward him, only those escape and have no part of punishment who have been sealed with a good seal and sprinkled with the blood of Christ. For you learned (him) saying: 'Amen amen I say to you, the one chewing my flesh and drinking my blood has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life; but the one not believing will not see life, but the wrath of God will remain on him.' Therefore partakers of eternal life, and friends and acquaintances to God and Father, and stronger than death, (are) the sanctified, through partaking of Christ, clearly in the mystical manner, and anointed with the holy blood. And he says very well that they must hasten unceasingly to complete the law about this. For we will cease, not at all from feasting in Christ, making leaven disappear from our own borders, that is, from all the land in which we might have our dwellings. For it will be necessary for those called through faith into the justification through Christ, feasting spiritually, not to do this in leaven of malice and wickedness, but rather cleaning out the old leaven to be remolded toward the better, and to be seen already somehow a new lump, with all the race and all the household, and those in all the country, through which is signified that the holy multitude of those who have received the faith is very great and countless. And the first day of the week he said must be called holy, and the seventh called holy, the law showing, I think, that: of the life of man the time at the beginning was holy, as in the forefather of the race Adam, not yet having broken the commands and disregarded the divine ordinances; and holy and much greater the one at the last, that is, the one in Christ, who is second Adam, refashioning the race from the things that happened in between into newness of life in spirit. And he enjoins that it is necessary also to keep sabbath on the seventh, departing from every work. For it would befit very fittingly those through faith having en(tered) (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: When these things have been carefully kept, and indeed carried through to the end as the lawgiver wished, he says that he will pass through and, as it were, go about the whole land of the Egyptians, destroying the firstborn and executing judgment on the gods of the Egyptians; that is, he will exact a penalty from all that was lofty and exalted among them and ranked all but among the objects of worship because of its glory, for so harsh and lawless a mind and for overweening arrogance. But he promised to shelter the sons of Israel, since their lintels had been smeared with the blood, which he also called a sign of their belonging to him: ‘For I will see the sign,’ he says, ‘and I will shelter you’ (Exodus 12:13). For when God brings wrath and anger on everything lofty and high, as the prophet's word has it (Isaiah 2:12), and condemns to death the wanton sinner who has endlessly neglected reverence toward him, only those escape and have no share in the punishment who have been sealed with the good seal and sprinkled with the blood of Christ. For you have heard him say: ‘Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life (John 6:54), and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life (John 5:24); but whoever does not believe will not see life, but the wrath of God will remain on him’ (John 3:36). So those who have been sanctified through partaking of Christ, in the mystical manner of course, and anointed with the holy blood, are sharers in eternal life, friends and intimates of God the Father, and stronger than death.

He says, and very well, that they must press on without ceasing to carry out the law on this point. For surely we shall not cease from keeping feast in Christ as we remove leaven from our own borders, that is, from all the land in which we spend our days. For those called through faith to the justification that comes through Christ, as they keep feast spiritually, must not do this in the leaven of malice and wickedness; rather, they must clean out the old leaven (1 Corinthians 5:7–8), be refashioned for the better, and be seen already, in some way, as a new lump, with all their kin and all their household, and those in all the land; by which it is signified that the holy multitude of those who have received the faith is great and beyond counting.

He said that the first day of the week must be called holy, and the seventh too a holy convocation. By this, I think, the law shows that in the life of man the time at the beginning was holy, as in Adam, the forefather of the race, before he had broken what was commanded and disregarded the divine precepts; and holy, and much greater, is the time at the end, that is, the time in Christ, who is the second Adam, refashioning the race, from what had happened in between, into newness of life in the Spirit. choices.term: Καταλήξομεν γὰρ, οὔτι που τοῦ ἑορτάζειν ἐπὶ Χριστῷ
choices.english: For surely we shall not cease from keeping feast in Christ
choices.why: οὔτι που negates the verb; ties to 'without ceasing' in the sentence before.
Cyril joins three Johannine sayings into one; each part is cited beside its words.
Old English dropped it ('marked with the blood of the true Lamb').
